## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix option parsing before merge because a pathless `--json` blocks report generation when it precedes `--junit`.

## Changes

The pull request adds `--json` with an optional destination that defaults to `results.json`. It adds a writer for the requested reports and tests for JSON destinations and the required JUnit path.

## Critical

- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Keep following flags out of the JSON path — With `--json --junit out.xml`, the parser consumes `--junit` as the JSON path and rejects `out.xml` as an unknown option. The JSON branch treats any following token as a path. — Users who request default JSON output before JUnit get neither report. — Fix: Apply the JUnit branch’s `--` prefix check when deciding whether to consume the next token.

## Important

- app/cli.py:30 — correctness — Reject a shared JSON and JUnit destination — With `--junit out.xml --json out.xml`, the writer saves both reports to the same file. The second `write_text` call replaces the first report. — The call returns successfully with JSON in `out.xml`, and the requested JUnit report is lost. — Fix: Check for duplicate destinations before writing either report.

## Suggestions

- app/cli.py:29 — tests — Test writing both reports in one invocation — With `--junit out.xml --json out.json`, no test exercises the second iteration of the write loop. The only test that calls `write_reports` supplies one destination. — A regression that drops the second report would pass the tests.
